Lengths of stay: their distribution and its fit

Source: R/stkflw.R
lostay.Rd

The lengths of stay of a set of placements (or of people): the mean with its t interval, the median and quartiles, the longest; the share of stays in each band and at or below each threshold (15 days, the Mandela Rules' limit, say), with the share of each band carrying a flag (no review on record); and the fit of lognormal, exponential and Pareto laws by maximum likelihood, compared by AIC: a heavy tail (Pareto or lognormal beating the exponential) separates a few long stays from many short ones. A stay still open is a lower bound on its length; see losbnd() for the mean it bounds.

Usage

lostay(days, w = NULL, breaks = NULL, thr = NULL, flag = NULL, level = 0.95)

Arguments

days

The stays: numbers from 0.

w

NULL, or how many stays each value stands for: whole numbers from 0 with a positive total.

breaks

NULL, or band edges, increasing; a band is (lo, hi].

thr

NULL, or thresholds: numbers from 0.

flag

NULL, or TRUE/FALSE for each stay.

level

The level of the interval of the mean: one number between 0 and 1.

Value

An object of class lostay, a list: stay, a named vector (n, days, mean, sd, median, q1, q3, max, se, lo, hi); bands (with breaks: lo, hi, n, share of all stays, with flag flagged the share of the band's stays); thr (thr, atmost, above); fit (model, aic, best; the fits use the stays above 0); and par (meanlog, sdlog, alpha).

References

Clauset, A., Shalizi, C. R. and Newman, M. E. J. (2009). Power-law distributions in empirical data. SIAM Review, 51(4), 661-703. doi:10.1137/070710111

Examples

set.seed(3)
s <- round(rlnorm(400, 2.3, 1.1)) + 1
r <- lostay(s, breaks = c(0, 5, 15, 31, 61, Inf), thr = 15)
r$bands
#>   lo  hi   n  share
#> 1  0   5  93 0.2325
#> 2  5  15 157 0.3925
#> 3 15  31  84 0.2100
#> 4 31  61  43 0.1075
#> 5 61 Inf  23 0.0575
r$fit
#>         model      aic  best
#> 1   lognormal 3105.502  TRUE
#> 2 exponential 3228.711 FALSE
#> 3      pareto 3249.590 FALSE
